title: Battle of Plassey
disclaimer: Schematic, not a survey. The Bhagirathi has shifted since 1757.

map.attribution: Original schematic drawn for this project. North is up. The Bhagirathi is diagrammatic and has changed course since 1757. The mango grove and the Nawab's camp are attested areas. The ditch and hunting lodge are traditional landmarks placed approximately. Marker dots are not surveyed points. Movement arrows are illustrative. Do not replace this plate with a scanned or traced published map.

scenes.title: Armies assemble
scenes.narration: 23 June 1757. About 3,000 Company soldiers face Siraj ud-Daulah. His host is near 50,000.
scenes.speech: Twenty third of June, seventeen fifty seven. Three thousand Company soldiers face Siraj ud Dowlah. His host is near fifty thousand.

scenes.title: The battle begins
scenes.narration: Mir Madan and the French guns engage. Mir Jafar's division, promised the throne, does not.
scenes.speech: Mir Madan and the French guns engage. Mir Jafar's division, promised the throne, does not.

scenes.title: Rain and the turning point
scenes.narration: A midday downpour soaks the field. Company gunners have covered their powder. Their guns reopen, and Mir Madan is killed.
scenes.speech: A midday downpour soaks the field. Company gunners have covered their powder. Their guns reopen, and Mir Madan is killed.

scenes.title: Siraj ud-Daulah withdraws
scenes.narration: Siraj ud-Daulah withdraws toward Murshidabad. The route on this map is illustrative.
scenes.speech: Siraj ud Dowlah withdraws toward Murshidabad. The route on this map is illustrative.

scenes.title: Political consequences
scenes.narration: Clive reported twenty-two killed. Siraj was overthrown. Mir Jafar was made Nawab.
scenes.speech: Clive reported twenty two killed. Siraj was overthrown. Mir Jafar was made Nawab.

lines: Losses were small beside the result

sources.text: The battle was fought on 23 June 1757 at Palashi (Plassey), on the Bhagirathi in Bengal, between Calcutta and Murshidabad. The river has since moved. This map is an original schematic, not a surveyed plan and not a copy of a published battle map.

Company strength is about 3,000: commonly listed as roughly 750 European infantry, 100 topasses, 2,100 sepoys, gunners and sailors, with eight field pieces and two howitzers. Published totals vary by a few hundred. The Nawab's host is a contemporary estimate near 50,000, including a large cavalry and dozens of guns, plus a French party of about 40 to 50 men under St. Frais. Much of that host did not fight.
refs: Commonly repeated order of battle, cross-checked with Britannica

sources.text: Mir Jafar agreed to support Clive in return for the nawabship and did not engage. Rai Durlabh, Yar Lutuf Khan, and the Jagat Seths were also part of the intrigue. His position on the map is an approximate flank, not a surveyed coordinate.

A midday downpour is part of the standard account. Company gunners kept powder under tarpaulins, and the Company guns fired again afterward. Mir Madan, who remained loyal to Siraj, was killed. Historians still debate how decisive the rain was beside the conspiracy. The death is attested; the dot is not the surveyed spot where he fell.
refs: World History Encyclopedia, Battle of Plassey
The Past, A victory of significance: The Battle of Plassey, 23 June 1757

sources.text: Clive's report, widely repeated, gives 22 killed and about 50 wounded on the Company side. Some later compilations list 27 killed. Clive estimated about 500 killed and wounded on the Nawab's side. These are contemporary figures, not a modern count. The narration attributes the figure of 22 to Clive's report.
refs: Clive's casualty return as repeated in later histories

sources.text: Siraj left the field toward Murshidabad. The route drawn on the map is illustrative. He was later captured and killed. Mir Jafar was installed as Nawab. The Company's Diwani, the right to collect Bengal's revenue, was granted in 1765 after the Battle of Buxar, not at Plassey. A short pursuit is part of the standard narrative and is not drawn, so the withdrawal arrow stays readable.
